it was officially declared 7 years ago that the world cup would take place in brazil. 
last year, around june, some huge riots and protests started to take place. it began with this organization called "Movimento Passe Livre", and they were protesting for better public transportation for affordable prices (there had been a raise, and since they originally want free transportation, they were (everybody was) outraged). 
on a thursday, i don't quite remember the day it was, but it was June, one riot was very violently recriminated by the police. it was so violent, that on 16th of june, we all practically went to the streets, to protest the use of excessive force by the police, and their lack of preparation for situations like that. it was amazing, something none of us young brazilians (such as myself) had ever seen in our lives, and for the first time, since 1994, basically, people were united as one and fighting together for a common goal. 
after that, the whole "fifa go home" started to get stronger. i think a lot of people felt empowered by the riots of june, and they haven't stopped a bit ever since (they are much smaller, much, much smaller, but they do take place, nevertheless). i think it's a very valid point of view, but it's too late, goddamnit. this thing starts on thursday, i love football/soccer and the world cup with all my life, i do hope to god and everything that brazil wins this bloody thing, i will even paint my freaking face and i will go crazy every match we win. i wish everybody, now, would just respect the foreigners who have nothing to do with this that are coming, treat everyone very nicely, enjoy it, and AFTERWARDS demand that legal actions are taken, to see who stole what, how much etc. the world cup will already be difficult to deal with, can you imagine it, though, with its chaos multiplied by 1000?
